mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the predicted negative returns are not statistically distinguishable from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the correlation between GDPC1 decline and SPX returns is not significant at the 1% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenues and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the relationship reverses during periods of strong export demand.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary policy tightening in the face of rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both proxies exceed their 12-month averages, or the effect reverses during periods of strong economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid month-over-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) above the previous six-month average signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 6-mo moving average and > previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive following triggered events, or the effect is absent during periods of high mortgage rates.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE signals a labor market expansion with low unemployment, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases YoY and UNRATE < 5% simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive when both proxies co-move in this way, or the relationship breaks down during periods of wage inflation above 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) over four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue expectations for consumer-facing firms and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during four-month periods of sustained retail sales decline, or the effect reverses during periods of strong online retail growth.
